title: West Liberty Tornado Recovery
description: Soldiers and Airmen of the Kentucky National Guard rush to the aid of tornado-ravaged West Liberty, Ky.  Soldiers of the 301st Chemical Co. conduct patrols to help look for any survivors who may be buried in the rubble. Available in high definition. Includes sound bites from Staff Sgt. Johnnie Patrick, 301st Chemical Co..
keywords: tornado, disaster recovery, "301st Chemical Co.", National Guard, Kentucky

transcript.text: On Friday evening, the eastern Kentucky town of West Liberty was rocked by a tornado that left the town in ruins.
Shortly after the winds died down, the men and women of the Kentucky National Guard arrived to help with the recovery efforts.
Coming from across the Commonwealth, engineers, medics, and emergency specialists rushed to the shocking scene.
Soldiers from the 301st Chemical Company walked the streets of West Liberty and inspected the ruins for any survivors who might be still trapped in the rubble.
We're checking the perimeter of all these buildings that we can't enter because it's unsafe for the soldier.
We're looking around the debris that's on the edge of the outskirts of the building just to see it freaking.
Maybe help someone that might be trapped or need some attention real quick.
In the more eyes we got on it, the more chance we had to find it people.
These soldiers combed through the destruction using specialized cameras to look into collapsed structures and to sense the heat of trapped victims.
As you can tell these guys down here, they've got some special tools that help us identify heat signatures and things of that nature too.
So if we can't get in, it's not safe for us to get in, we have tools to put in there so we can see inside.
Sergeant Patrick and his fellow soldiers and airmen of the Kentucky National Guard continue to help the citizens of West Liberty pick up the pieces.
Both here and at four other locations across the state, the Kentucky National Guard continues to provide aid wherever it is needed.
For the 133rd Mobile Public Affairs Detachment, I'm Army Staff Sergeant Aaron Heiler.
